sections.title: Sound of Y
paragraphs: The letter name is (Y) /j/. Its main sound is heard in the word (yes) /jɛs/, which expresses agreement. This letter makes four different sounds in English.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Raise the middle of your tongue close to the hard roof of your mouth. Keep your lips relaxed and let your voice turn on. For the next sound, open your mouth wide and glide your tongue up and forward. For the third sound, raise your tongue high and spread your lips wide. For the last sound, lower your tongue slightly. Put a hand on your throat to feel the voice buzz.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: At the start of a syllable before a vowel, it sounds as in (yes) /jɛs/. In a stressed syllable at the end of a short word, it sounds as in (my) /maɪ/. At the end of a longer word without stress, it sounds as in (happy) /hæ.pi/. In a closed stressed syllable of Greek origin, it sounds as in (gym) /dʒɪm/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not block the air with your tongue when you start a word. If you press your tongue against the roof of your mouth, it sounds like j in jam. Keep the air flowing smoothly without any friction. Do not drop the sound before vowels. Hold the glide firmly so the start stays clear.
